summary: Well-targeted and self-diagnosing: at bs<32 master's profile has ~9 extra at::native launches (about 20-29 us at bs=1) and no _post_expert_norm_weighted_sum_kernel, while at bs>=32 the Triton kernel runs and the glue is gone. Replacing exactly that call with one Triton launch either removes the glue (a gain) or leaves it in the profile (a flat that is clearly not the post-norm), so a single run can be read without companions.
justification: Plausible. The full master profile (fb2cc736613747df) supports it more strongly than the hypothesis says. bs=32 lists only 7 kernels in total: 2 Marlin, align, _post_expert_norm_weighted_sum_kernel 4.1us, index_elementwise (the expert_map gather), act_and_mul, and one unrolled_elementwise. bs=1/8/16 list 16 kernels each ('12 + 4 more'), and _post_expert_norm_weighted_sum_kernel does not appear down to the 1.0-1.2us rows. A Triton kernel that costs 4.1us at bs=32 would not drop below 1.2us at bs=16, so it really is gone. In its place are reduce_kernel<512,1>, reduce_kernel<128,4> (4.3-4.7us, which the hypothesis does not count), elementwise_kernel<128,2> x3, elementwise_kernel<128,4>, unrolled_elementwise x2, two vectorized_elementwise, and more. At bs=1: 78.1us total, minus Marlin 41.1, align 4.4, act 1.5 and index 1.8, leaves about 29us of glue, and some of it is not post-norm (the one unrolled_elementwise that is also present at bs=32). The ~16us estimate is therefore conservative; the real bound is about 20-25us at bs=1. The work is tiny: at most 64 KB at bs=1 and 1 MB at bs=16, still in L2 because w2 just wrote it. One launch per token at 8 warps with BLOCK_H=4096 (16 fp32 acc regs per thread) should take 2-4us. The direction and size fit TASK.md. All six loads have equal weight, so gains of roughly +12-18% at decode_1 and +8-12% at verify_1 and decode_16 would put the geomean near 1.04-1.05x, well outside the ±1.5% drift. SGLang's baseline pays the same eager path, so the paired ratio benefits fully. Weakest link: the attribution is inferred, and the M<32 boundary is also where block_size_m changes (bs=1/8/16 pick block_size_m=8; bs=32 picks 16). Some of the reduce/elementwise launches could come from the Marlin or align wrappers' block-8 path rather than the post-norm wrapper. Against that, those wrappers' own kernels (Marlin x2, small_batch align) appear at every size, and the post-norm kernel's absence is direct evidence. The profile after the change settles it either way. Minor: SGLang's wrapper threshold is unknown (anywhere in 17..32), so the <32 cut is safe but may not be tight.
confounders: sglang-marlin-path-parity: this is the base, not a confounder. It introduced the fused_post_expert_norm_weighted_sum call being replaced and the block_size_m rule that switches from 8 to 16 at the same M=32 boundary. The change touches only the final combine, and Marlin's output y is identical either way, so a gain cannot come from an interaction. The only confusion it adds is in attribution, and the post-change profile resolves that (whether the at::native reduce/elementwise launches remain at bs=1/8/16).
interference: No companion warranted. A gain means the replaced call's eager glue is gone, and the profile shows which launches vanished. A flat or loss with the glue still present means it came from elsewhere (Marlin/align block-8 wrapper), and the hypothesis already records that. A flat or loss with the glue gone means the new kernel is slow, and its own top_kernels time shows that directly. bs>=32 is an in-run control for drift. An ab-revert of the only landed hypothesis would remove the Marlin path altogether, which makes no sense. An ab-tune of block_size_m belongs to the queued marlin-block-size-m-* hypotheses. The split-H variant is correctly deferred as a follow-up ab-tune, to run only if the kernel itself measures slow.
rules_flags: No rule problem as written. Branching on num_tokens (shape) is allowed. Allocating the output with torch.empty((M,H)) is shape-driven and matches what master already does. There are no host syncs, and the eid>=0 test is an in-kernel scalar branch, not a host branch on input values.

Keep the weight rule: store the original bf16 post_norm_w in state (prepare needs a new state['post_norm_w'] = weights['post_norm_w'] entry; master only has state['norm_w']) and form 1+w in fp32 in registers. Do NOT store a precomputed fp32 (1+w) tensor in prepare(); that would be a weight kept at a different precision.
Activations: y (bf16 from Marlin) is read and the output written as bf16, with fp32 math only in registers. This matches SGLang's BF16 boundaries.
open_questions: Do the reduce_kernel<512,1>, reduce_kernel<128,4> and elementwise_kernel<128,2> launches vanish at bs=1/8/16 after the change? Record the full kernel list (including the '4 more') in the attempt file. That separates post-norm glue from block-size-8 Marlin/align wrapper glue.
If it gains: the same kernel could replace SGLang's Triton call at bs>=32 (4.1-6.5us), but only as a separate hypothesis, since the gain would be under 1.5% per shape and hard to resolve.

The bs=4 test exercises tokens that have no local slot, and bs=1 can have zero local slots. Confirm the zero row is written explicitly (acc is stored even when every slot is skipped), so torch.empty garbage never reaches the output.
